reasoning.title: Aggregate at the requested entity level
reasoning.description: Use when a ranking asks for brands but the available Bestsellers report lists products; do not use this extra mapping workflow when a brand-specific report already displays aggregated brand totals.
reasoning.content: Open Reports → Products → Bestsellers, set the requested period and date range, select “Show Report,” and capture every displayed product and quantity—not just the leading or tied rows. Then use a brand-specific report if available; otherwise go to Catalog → Products, select “Clear all” to remove stale filters, search and execute “Search” for each exact product, verify its full Manufacturer/Brand value in the grid or detail view, and sum all quantities by brand before ranking; never infer a brand from a product name or stop because the top products tie.

reasoning.title: Aggregate the complete report at the requested entity level
reasoning.description: Use when a shopping_admin task asks for a top brand, manufacturer, or other grouping over a date range rather than merely the top individual product; direct product-ranking questions do not require brand-level aggregation.
reasoning.content: Open Reports → Products → Bestsellers (or the date-filterable Ordered Products Report), enter the full requested range, select “Show Report,” and capture every displayed product and quantity. If brands are not shown, use Catalog → Products, clear stale filters, search each exact product, and verify its full Manufacturer/Brand in the grid or detail view before summing quantities by brand and retaining every tie; do not stop at the leading product rows, infer brands from names, or confuse tied products with tied brands.

reasoning.title: Aggregate the complete Bestsellers report by requested type
reasoning.description: Use when asked for best-selling products or product types within a date range; do not use the Dashboard “Bestsellers” widget because it lists individual products and is not reliably filtered to the requested period.
reasoning.content: Open “Reports” → “Products” → “Bestsellers,” enter the inclusive “From” and “To” dates, click “Show Report,” and inspect every displayed row. If the question asks for a product type, classify near-identical products and size/color variants under their shared type, sum “Order Quantity” across all rows, verify all co-leaders, and report every tie; copy full visible labels, opening details if the grid abbreviates them, rather than guessing from names or counting exact-name repetitions.

reasoning.title: Aggregate bestseller rows at the requested product-type level
reasoning.description: Use when a question asks for best-selling product types or categories over a date range, rather than individual SKUs. Do not use the unfiltered Dashboard “Bestsellers” widget or treat the first SKU row as the requested type.
reasoning.content: Open “REPORTS” > “Products” > “Bestsellers,” set “Period,” “From,” and “To,” then select “Show Report.” Read or export every result row, open product details if a grid name is abbreviated, normalize near-identical variants to their common product type, sum “Order Quantity” by type, and rank those totals; report one type when one is requested, enumerating ties only when the aggregated type totals actually tie and the full values are visibly verified.

reasoning.title: Aggregate at the requested product granularity
reasoning.description: Use when a sales question asks for a product type, category, or family rather than an individual product; do not use this workflow when the requested entity is explicitly a product/SKU.
reasoning.content: Open “REPORTS” → “Products” → “Ordered,” apply the requested “From” and “To” range, and use all displayed ordered quantities; the dashboard “Bestsellers” widget and “REPORTS” → “Products” → “Bestsellers” are look-alikes that rank individual products and do not answer a type-level question directly. Map every sold product to its verified type using the product row/detail view, sum quantities across all variants of each type, then rank the totals; copy the full visible type label, distinguish near-identical types, and report every type tied at the qualifying rank rather than guessing from product names or returning tied products.

reasoning.title: Aggregate by the requested catalog field
reasoning.description: Use when a best-selling question asks for a product attribute or category-level field rather than an individual product; use the product-level ranking directly only when the requested entity is Product.
reasoning.content: Under “Reports” > “Products,” “Bestsellers” is a look-alike trap: “Period,” “From,” “To,” and “Show Report” filter sales, but the grid groups by Product, not Product Type. Read every result row and its full “Order Quantity,” resolve each distinct SKU through “Catalog” > “Products” or its detail view to copy the exact displayed Product Type, then sum quantities by that field and rank the totals; do not infer types by stripping variant suffixes or merging similar names. Verify the winning type from the completed aggregation, and enumerate every tied top group if ties exist.

reasoning.title: Aggregate SKU sales by requested product type
reasoning.description: Use when a Magento Admin question asks for a product type or category over a date range; do not use this procedure when the requested entity is an individual product or SKU.
reasoning.content: Navigate to Reports > Products > Bestsellers, set Period plus From/To, and select Show Report, but treat the resulting Product and Order Quantity rows as SKU-level data—not a type ranking. Read or export every result, open Catalog > Products product details when names are abbreviated or the type/category is unclear, map each distinct variant carefully, sum quantities by the requested type, and rank those totals; verify the winning label from visible catalog data and report every qualifying tie rather than guessing from the first SKU rows.

reasoning.title: Aggregate ordered variants by merchandise type
reasoning.description: Use when a task asks for the best-selling product or merchandise type over a date range; do not use this method when it explicitly asks for Magento entity types such as Simple or Configurable Product.
reasoning.content: Navigate to Reports > Products > Ordered, enter the full inclusive range, choose a Show By interval that aggregates the range, and click Refresh; the dashboard Bestsellers widget and Bestsellers report are look-alikes that may be unfiltered or show only a limited product ranking. Read every displayed product/SKU and Ordered Quantity row, map each distinct variant to its merchandise type, sum all variants by that type, and report every tied leader; never substitute the catalog Type column, infer from a few rows, or inspect Catalog > Products without first using Clear all to remove active filters. Verify the winning label from visible data, preserve near-identical variants, and open a product detail if the grid abbreviates the full name.

reasoning.title: Aggregate order lines at the requested product level
reasoning.description: Use when the question asks for a product type over a multi-period range; do not use this method when the requested answer is an individual SKU already represented by a report row.
reasoning.content: Navigate through “SALES” → “Orders,” filter the complete requested date range, open every qualifying order, and read all “Items Ordered” quantities; the dashboard “Bestsellers” widget and “REPORTS” → “Products” → “Bestsellers” are look-alikes that show product/variant leaders by interval, not quarter-wide product-type totals. Copy full item names from order details if a grid abbreviates them, normalize only genuine size/color/configuration variants into the same product type, sum every quantity across the full range, rank the totals, and report every top tie only after verifying the underlying rows rather than guessing from similar names.

reasoning.title: Aggregate by the requested product level
reasoning.description: Use when a task asks for a best-selling product type, category, or family over a date range; do not apply when it explicitly asks for an individual product or SKU.
reasoning.content: Navigate via “Reports” → “Products” → “Bestsellers,” set “From,” “To,” and “Period,” then select “Show Report”; note that this report ranks individual products and has no order-status filter, so it cannot directly answer a type-level or status-filtered question. Export the complete results if the grid shows only a subset, open product details when names are abbreviated, map near-identical variants to their verified type, sum “Order Quantity” across every product of that type, and rank those totals rather than treating tied SKU rows as the answer. Return the single visible highest aggregate, enumerating all ties only if the final type-level totals truly tie.

reasoning.title: Aggregate sales at the requested product level
reasoning.description: Use when a shopping-admin question asks for a best-selling product type/category rather than an individual product or SKU; do not use this aggregation when the task explicitly requests the top SKU or Magento’s technical catalog entity type.
reasoning.content: Open “Reports” → “Products” → “Bestsellers,” set the inclusive “From”/“To” range and “Period,” then select “Show Report”; this report ranks individual products and cannot directly answer type-level questions or questions requiring an unavailable status filter. Read or export every result row, use “Catalog” → “Products” or product details to verify each item’s full merchandise-type label, then sum “Order Quantity” across all genuine variants of each type and rank the totals—never infer the type by trimming names or confuse it with the catalog “Type” column, and report every tied leader only if the completed aggregation visibly confirms the tie.
